title: Sweet Basil Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Basil blitzed with half the sugar and steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla.
summary: Classic French custard with fresh basil blitzed into the sugar and steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla. Herbal, sweet and surprisingly refreshing.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make basil sugar
steps.text: Blitz the basil leaves with half the sugar until bright green and sandy. The sugar grinds the leaves, releasing their oils quickly.

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Warm the cream, milk, basil sugar and salt until steaming, then cover off the heat for 20 min.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: Beat the yolks and the rest of the sugar together in the heatproof bowl.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Rewarm the dairy, whisk two ladles into the yolks and pour back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on low, stirring steadily, to 77-80 °C, when the custard clings to the spatula. Gentle heat keeps the herb flavour fresh.

steps.title: Strain and chill
steps.text: Sieve, pressing on the basil, then cool quickly over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h. Fast cooling helps the base keep its fresh, green taste.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Use only the leaves and dry them well after washing.
A common mistake is steeping the basil for hours, which brings out a grassy, bitter edge; 20 min is plenty.
Serve with fresh strawberries for a lovely summer pudding.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 1 week; the basil flavour fades after that.
